messages.subject: Re: Error compiling model with user defined distribution
parts:
Hi Luiza,

Thanks for the reproducible example.  I also got an error message, but it was more informative:
Error: Type double of the return() argument does not match type integer given in the returnType() statement (void is default).

I'm not sure if we got different error messages because I am running on our development branch (devel) or not, but, just in case, please be sure you have the current version of nimble.

In any case, try changing "returnType(integer(1))" to "returnType(double(1))".  Although they are integer values, they will be treated as doubles and need to be declared that way.

Also, you may find it numerically advantageous in dBPois to do the main work on a log scale and then exponentiate at the end if log==FALSE.

-Perry


On Fri, May 31, 2019 at 1:09 PM Luiza Sette <luh....@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello, 

I'm a new user in nimble so I apologize if this is actually something simple!
I implemented the bivariate Poisson distribution (Lakshminarayana et al 1999) in but I'm getting an error when trying to compile a simple model that uses this distribution.
The error is the following:

Error: In sizeAssignAfterRecursing: 'rBPois' is not available or its output type is unknown.
 This occurred for: eigenBlock(model_y,getNodeFunctionIndexedInfo(ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__,1),1:2) <<- rBPois(=1,mu1=model_mu1[getNodeFunctionIndexedInfo(ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__,1)],
mu2=model_mu2[getNodeFunctionIndexedInfo(ARG1_INDEXEDNODEINFO__,1)],delta=model_delta[1])

The functions follow: 

#Distribution function
dBPois <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1), mu1 = double(), mu2 = double(),delta = double(0), log = logical(0, default = 0)) {
    c= 1-exp(-1)
    a = mu1^(x[1])*mu2^(x[2])*exp(-(mu1+mu2))
    b = (1+delta*(exp(-x[1])-exp(-c*mu1))*(exp(-x[2])-exp(-c*mu2)))
    prob = a*b/(factorial(x[1])*factorial(x[2]))
    if(log) return(log(prob))
    return(prob)
    returnType(double(0))
  })

#This function to return the cumulative and is used the the generation
Cdf <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(z = integer(0),y1 = integer(0), mu1 = double(), mu2 = double(), delta = double(0)) {
    c<- 1-exp(-1)
    y2_aux<-0;cond<-0;
    s<-0
    while(y2_aux<=z){
      cond <- mu2^(y2_aux)*exp(-mu2)*(1+delta*((exp(-y1)-exp(-c*mu1))*(exp(-y2_aux)-exp(-c*mu2))))
      cond <- cond/factorial(y2_aux)
      s <- s+cond
      y2_aux <- y2_aux+1
    }
    returnType(double(0))
    return((s))
  })

#Random generator
rBPois <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(n = integer(0), mu1 = double(), mu2 = double(), delta = double(0)) {
    y1_aux <- rpois(1,lambda = mu1)
    #z <- numeric(0)
    u <- runif(1,0,1)
    if(u < Cdf(z=0,y1_aux,mu1,mu2,delta)){
      y2_aux <- 0
    } else{
      # while loop to determine which subinterval,I, you are in
      # terminated when B = 2
      B <- 100
      I <- 0
      while(B == 100){
        # the interval to check
        int1 <- Cdf(I,y1_aux,mu1,mu2,delta)
        int2 <- Cdf(I+1,y1_aux,mu1,mu2,delta)
        # see if the uniform is in that interval
        if( (u> int1) & (u < int2) ){# if so, quit the while loop and store the value
          y2_aux <- I+1
          B = 2
        } else {
          # If not, continue the while loop and increase I by 1
          I<-I+1
        }
        if (I > 1000){
          stop("Too many iterations.")
        }
      }
      
    }
    result = c(y1_aux,y2_aux)
    returnType(integer(1))
    return(result)
  })

and the model:

code2 <- nimbleCode({
  mu1 ~ dgamma(1,1)
  mu2 ~ dgamma(1,1)
  delta ~ dunif(-1,1)
  for(i in 1:N){
  y[i,1:2] ~ dBPois(mu1,mu2,delta)
  }  
})

I'm passing some random data to test the model as:

constants= list(N = 100)
data = list(y= matrix(rpois(100,2),nrow = 100,ncol=2))
inits <- list(delta = 0, mu1 = 1, mu2 =1)

model2 <- nimbleModel(code2, constants = constants,
                      data = data,
                      check = TRUE,inits=inits)

This piece runs fine as well as "model2$calculate() " but the error appears when I run:

model2 <- compileNimble(model2, showCompilerOutput = TRUE, resetFunctions = TRUE)

I realize the error is about something in the generating function but I can't figure it out.
I tried to change return type to matrix and things like that but it end up producing the same error.

Any help would be much appreciated :)
